label: <DEL> step of short / x-or-l-initial sequences, plus first early input e
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) The delimiter step (recall_idx 0): 77% of activation mass, and all of the strongest activations (e.g. x p v s <DEL>). It fires on 6.8% of <DEL> steps, more often for short sequences (L=3: 5.5x lift, L=4: 3.1x) and when the first original token is x or l (first_tok x/l together carry about 41% of mass). Which <DEL> steps fire is only partly predictable, because it depends on sequence content (x, l, s, p tokens) beyond these conditions. (2) Input token e during the original phase, mostly its first occurrence and early in the sequence (t=0 is the most frequent case; activations are weaker at t=0 and larger at t=1-4). This gives 22% of mass at low to mid magnitude. It almost never fires during the copy phase (0.8% of mass), on repeated e, or on any other input token. Dev scores: P=0.30, R=0.84, mass recall 0.85; precision is low because most short-sequence <DEL> steps and early e inputs do not fire.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, l, p, z, o, n; least: k, 0, t, w) and the current input token, by step (t=0: e; t=1: e; t=2: e); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=10, L=7 & t=8, recall_idx=1.
